AI could actually wipe out the entire human race within the next couple of years, and this has been said by researchers from OpenAI and Anthropic themselves.

I wish I could say more 👀

I choose the difficult road every single time.

Not because it makes a better story, but because the person I’m becoming can only be built in places most people are unwilling to go.

I’ve been overlooked. I’ve been lost. I’ve made choices that made no sense to the people around me, and I had to carry the pressure of those decisions by myself.

There were nights when the only thing keeping me moving was the version of myself I could see in my head. A man who didn’t exist yet, but felt more real to me than my current reality.

Instead of letting that distance destroy me, I turned it into motivation.

I didn’t have a large circle. I didn’t have a safety net. I didn’t have people constantly reminding me that everything would work out.

I just had the belief that quitting would hurt more than continuing.

Three years later, the decision to keep going has taken me to places I once believed were only available to people born with the right connections, opportunities, or advantages.

I built this one decision at a time while most people were still waiting for the perfect moment to begin.

This is what happens when you refuse to abandon yourself.

Not for a week. Not for a few months. Not only when things are going well.

Every single day, for years, without any guarantee that the work would eventually pay off.

My circle is still small, but I’m deeply grateful for the people who believed in me when none of this existed outside of an idea.

We are only getting started.

I’ve been obsessed with this for years now.

Not casually interested.

Obsessed.

To me, growing a business is a lot like chess.

Most people focus on the move in front of them.

More ads.
More content.
A new website.
A new offer.

But growth is rarely decided by one move.

It’s decided by how every move positions the next one.

I’ve spent years studying that.

How a business positions itself.
How it earns attention.
How it converts that attention into revenue.
How marketing decisions compound when the strategy behind them is right.

I’ve worked with hundreds of clients.

Taught over 3,000 students.

Built businesses to $1M+ months.

And through all of it, I became less interested in isolated tactics and more interested in the entire board.

Where is the leverage?

What is being overlooked?

What should happen now so the business is in a stronger position three moves from now?

That is the part I love.

I’m naturally all in; or nothing.

When I want to understand something, I lock myself in until I do.

I study hard.

I test.

I refine.

I pay attention to the small decisions that most people dismiss, because those are often the decisions that separate a business that looks busy from one that is actually moving forward.

Today, my work is centered around growth.

Helping businesses sharpen their positioning, strengthen their marketing, and make better strategic decisions around how they acquire customers and scale.

Not chasing every new tactic.

Not making moves just to feel productive.

Making the right moves, in the right order, for the right reason.

That is what makes this interesting to me.

Every business is a different board.

Different constraints.

Different opportunities.

Different winning positions.

My job is to see the board clearly and help create the path forward.

I love what I do.

I love the strategy behind it.

And I love helping ambitious people get closer to the business they originally imagined building.

Still obsessed.

Still studying.

Checkmate.
